correctness.rationale: An explicit Fano tangent-line argument proves every induced matching has at most three edges; the supplied seven-triplet partition proves χs=7. All 84 compatible triples are enumerated from 21 labelled flags, a least-uncovered-edge exact-cover procedure counts all 416 unordered partitions without duplicates, and every one of the 86,320 partition pairs is inspected for class overlaps. Distinct partitions share no five classes, exactly 1568 pairs share four, and all-source BFS proves one connected component with radius=diameter=6. The 336 automorphisms generated from 168 point collineations plus duality yield six orbits of sizes 8,16,56,112,112,112. Two actual independent source implementations (cyclic Fano Python, GF(2)^3 C++) rederive 84/416/0/1568 and diameter six. The finite classifications require the included programs; no inference from sampled data is made.

value.rationale: The problem naturally refines a classical known optimum on the Heawood graph, a highly symmetric cubic cage and Fano incidence geometry. It asks if distinct minimum interference-avoiding frequency assignments can be modified without temporarily increasing their seven channels. All 416 optima are frozen under two-class updates yet become connected with sharp six-step distance under three-class updates, a substantive rigidity/mobility threshold not implied by χs(H)=7. The six symmetry orbits and complete degree profile provide a natural test case and symmetry-level structural census. This is not the scalar-index recomputation or an arbitrary restriction of a larger known census; no claim of generalization to other graphs is needed.
